meta.name: USA true/false statements, 93 items (50 false, 43 true), disputed items removed
meta.source_prompt: Write fifty  untrue things about the USA and fifty true things about the USA.
meta.filtering: Items with a factual error, a contested ranking, or a territory-dependent reading were removed (see excluded_items). The remaining labels follow the generator's true/untrue sections and were spot-checked, not exhaustively fact-checked.

excluded_items.statement: The USA lies entirely in the Northern Hemisphere.
excluded_items.reason: All 50 states lie in the Northern Hemisphere, but the USA includes American Samoa south of the equator; the statement is ambiguous about territories.

excluded_items.statement: The USA is the third-largest country in the world by total area.
excluded_items.reason: Third-largest by total area is source-dependent; China is close and some sources rank the USA fourth.

excluded_items.statement: The national motto is "In God We Trust" (adopted 1956); "E Pluribus Unum" is also an official motto.
excluded_items.reason: In God We Trust is the official motto; E Pluribus Unum is a de facto motto, so calling both official is disputed.

excluded_items.statement: The Missouri River is the longest river in the USA.
excluded_items.reason: Missouri and Mississippi river lengths are close and the longest-river ranking differs by measurement source.

excluded_items.statement: The national tree of the USA is the oak (designated 1954).
excluded_items.reason: Congress designated the oak the national tree in 2004 (P.L. 108-447), not 1954.

excluded_items.statement: The diamond is the national gemstone of the USA (designated 1999).
excluded_items.reason: The United States has no federal national gemstone; diamond is Arkansas's state gemstone (1967).

excluded_items.statement: The square dance is the national dance of the USA (designated 1976).
excluded_items.reason: Square dance was designated the national folk dance for 1982-1983 only (P.L. 97-188); the 1976 date is wrong.
